from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = [
            "Superposition describes overlapping wave disturbances.",
            "Coherent light maintains constant phase relationships.",
            "Interference creates stable constructive patterns."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Nature of Wave Interference", lines)
        
        # Define objects
        wave1 = Wave(color=BLUE)
        wave2 = Wave(color=RED)
        sum_wave = Wave(color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_in_area(wave1, 'A1', 'B6', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(wave2, 'C1', 'D6', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(Create(wave1), Create(wave2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        # Simulated "coherent" state visualization (phasor arrows)
        phasor1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.5, color=BLUE)
        phasor2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.5, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(phasor1, 'C3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(phasor2, 'C4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(phasor1), Create(phasor2))
        self.play(Rotate(phasor1, angle=PI, about_point=phasor1.get_start()), 
                  Rotate(phasor2, angle=PI, about_point=phasor2.get_start()))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_in_area(sum_wave, 'E1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(VGroup(wave1, wave2), sum_wave))
        self.wait(2)

class Wave(VMobject):
    def __init__(self, color=WHITE, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.set_points_smoothly([np.array([x, np.sin(x*2), 0]) for x in np.linspace(-2, 2, 20)])
        self.set_color(color)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism of Diffraction", [
            "Diffraction occurs when waves encounter apertures.",
            "Huygens-Fresnel explains spreading wave behavior.",
            "Gratings map spatial information through diffraction."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent aperture and waves
        slit = Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=GREY).set_stroke(width=8)
        self.place_at_grid(slit, 'D2', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        wave_animation = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=0.2+i*0.2, angle=PI/2, start_angle=-PI/4, color=BLUE) for i in range(5)])
        self.place_at_grid(wave_animation, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(slit))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(wave_animation))
        self.play(wave_animation.animate.scale(2).shift(RIGHT*1.5))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Huygens Principle (Multiple source points)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        sources = VGroup(*[Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(slit.get_center() + UP*i*0.2) for i in [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]])
        self.play(FadeIn(sources))
        
        wavefronts = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW, stroke_opacity=0.5).move_to(s.get_center()) for s in sources])
        self.play(Create(wavefronts))
        self.play(wavefronts.animate.scale(2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Grating representation
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        grating = VGroup(*[Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=WHITE).shift(RIGHT*i*0.2) for i in range(-2, 3)])
        self.place_at_grid(grating, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        screen = Line(UP*1.5, DOWN*1.5, color=GREY).shift(RIGHT*3)
        self.play(FadeIn(grating), FadeIn(screen))
        
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=GREEN).move_to(screen.get_center() + UP*i*0.4) for i in [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]])
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.wait(1)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Nature of Wave Interference
sections.content: Briefly review the principle of superposition. Explain how two coherent light waves (same frequency, constant phase) meet to form an interference pattern of constructive and destructive peaks.
sections.example: Visualizing two stones dropped in a pond: how their circular ripples overlap to create a stationary pattern of 'highs' and 'lows'.

sections.title: The Mechanism of Diffraction
sections.content: Explain Huygens-Fresnel principle. Diffraction occurs when light encounters an obstacle or aperture, causing it to spread out. Introduce the concept of a diffraction grating as a tool to map spatial information.
sections.example: A laser pointer shining through a thin slit, creating a spread-out pattern of dots on a wall, where the distance between dots relates to the slit width.

sections.title: Holography: Recording the Wavefront
sections.content: Differentiate between photography (records intensity/amplitude only) and holography (records phase and amplitude). Show the 'reference beam' vs. the 'object beam' interference pattern recorded on a plate.
sections.example: An 'Optic Spy Camera' that records not just a 2D image, but the complex 'echo' of light waves bouncing off a 3D object.

sections.title: Reconstruction: The Diffraction Gate
sections.content: Explain that the hologram acts as a complex diffraction grating. When the reference light hits the plate, it is diffracted by the microscopic interference patterns to reconstruct the original 3D wavefront.
sections.example: A holographic 'Cyber-Pet' emerging from a flat card; when light hits the card, the diffraction pattern 'unfolds' the light into a 3D creature floating in mid-air.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Synthesize how diffraction and interference enable data storage and 3D imaging. Conclude with the importance of coherent light (lasers) in this process.
sections.example: Banknote security features: tilting a bill to see the color-shifting diffraction pattern that proves the holographic authenticity of the currency.
